selection_reasoning: Mining carrots is a straightforward, observable, and verifiable task that doesn't require deep Minecraft domain knowledge. The agent needs to find and break carrot crops in the scene. This task is easy to set up (place carrot crops in a farm setting), clearly verifiable (check if carrots appear in inventory), and provides a good atomic benchmark for testing an agent's ability to identify, navigate to, and interact with a specific block type. It's more interesting than simple 'find' tasks because it requires the agent to perform an action (mining/breaking) rather than just navigating, while still being a single atomic task.

milestones.description: Uses inventory_has because mining mature carrot crops causes carrot items to drop into the player's inventory. The block is 'minecraft:carrots' (plural) but the dropped item is 'minecraft:carrot' (singular). Fully mature crops (age=7) drop 2-5 carrots each, so mining even one crop guarantees at least 1 carrot in inventory. The player starts with an empty inventory, so any carrot present confirms successful mining. inventory_has is the preferred rule type (#1 in preference order) for mine tasks since the mined drop ends up in inventory.

scene_description: A fenced carrot farm on a cleared flat grass area, approximately 3-8 blocks east of spawn. The farm has a 4x5 plot of mature carrots (age=7) on hydrated farmland, surrounded by oak fences with an open gate facing the player. A water source block in the center keeps farmland hydrated.
task_text: Walk to the carrot farm ahead of you, enter through the open gate, and mine the carrot crops to collect carrots.
design_notes: The farm is placed 3-8 blocks east of spawn on a cleared 20x20 area. The /fill air command clears trees and obstacles above ground level. Grass_block provides a flat walking surface. Carrot crops are at age=7 (fully mature) so they drop carrots when broken by hand (no tools needed). The open fence gate faces the player for easy entry. Water at ~5,~-1,~0 keeps farmland hydrated; it replaces one farmland block so the carrot above it breaks on load, leaving ~19 intact plants.
